$comment: Config for Layer 2 of the sanitize gate (tools/particulars.js) — org/person/narrative particulars. Every value here is generic on purpose: this file ships in a public artefact, so it must not name anyone's org, people, or projects. YOUR particulars go in `.overlay/particulars` (gitignored, instance-owned, one term per line, `re:` prefix for a regex) — the substrate never learns them.
$comment_no_skip_paths: There is NO skip_paths key, and adding one back would be a mistake. A directory-wide skip is an unconditional escape hatch over a directory that ships publicly: anything dropped inside passes green, including the particulars this layer exists to catch. Fixtures that must carry particular-SHAPED content are handled two narrower ways instead — an inline `sanitize:allow` marker on the one line, or `expect_findings` below.
$comment_instance_paths: The instance set from DISTRIBUTION.md. Excluded only under `--substrate` scope (what `contribute` should use), and the gate names that narrowing in its summary line. The default whole-tree scope scans them too — a public artefact's example garden must be as clean as its machinery.
$comment_inline_marker: The ONLY whole-line suppression, and the one a human typed onto that line on purpose. Suppressions show up in the diff, which is the only thing keeping them honest.
$comment_marker_max_line: The budget that stops 'clears the line' from meaning 'clears the file'. A file with no newlines — minified JS, one-line JSON — is a SINGLE line, so one marker in it used to silence every rule over the whole file. Above this many characters the marker is refused and the line is scanned anyway; findings on a refused line say so. 300 is about three soft-wrapped terminal lines: the edge of what a reviewer reads, far below any bundle.
$comment_allow_substrings: Scoped to the matched SPAN, not the line. `example.com` clears the email match in `user@example.com`; it does not clear a person, an org namespace, a sum, or a declared particular sitting elsewhere on the same line. A whole-line allowlist is a kill switch wearing a per-rule label.
$comment_expect_findings: INVERTED fixtures: exact repo-relative paths (never prefixes — a prefix rebuilds the escape hatch) whose findings are expected and do not fail the gate. Their SILENCE fails it instead: a listed file that produces no findings, or that has vanished from the scan, exits 1. This is how a fixture holds particular-shaped content without carving a blind spot.
$comment_declared: Inline alternative to `.overlay/particulars`, for operators who prefer config. Leave empty upstream.
$comment_semantic: OPT-IN and never load-bearing. Set `command` to an argv array; file content arrives on stdin, and the command should print {"flagged": bool, "reasons": [...]}. Unset, missing, or failing = silently not run, and the deterministic rules above still carry the gate. Never rely on this lane alone.
